# `silk/logger`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Typed semantic logging with replaceable stdout and bounded in-memory providers.

## When to use
Require [`Logger`](#Logger) when code emits whole semantic messages but should not choose storage or
destination. Provide `silk.os_logger.StdoutLogger` at a native process edge. Use [`InMemoryLogger`](#InMemoryLogger) for
deterministic observation and failure tests.

## Details
Each invocation carries one [`LogLevel`](#LogLevel), one static format template, and one borrowed argument
pack. Providers reuse `silk.format` to produce one semantic message without adding caller-visible
Writer or allocation requirements. The in-memory provider retains at most eight committed events
and 64 message bytes, and exposes attempted calls separately from successful commits.

## Gotchas
Logger failures are typed [`LogError`](#LogError) values and do not guarantee that a message committed.
In-memory accessors require an event index less than [`length`](#Logger.impl.length) and a valid message-byte index.

## Examples
### Record and inspect one warning

```silk
import silk.effect { Effect }

import silk.logger { Logger, LogError }
import silk.logger { LogLevel }

import silk.usize

effect fn program() -> i32
! LogError {
  let mut logger = Logger.inMemoryProvider()
  let logged = run Effect.logWarning("cache {kind} missed {count} times", &.{
    kind: "users",
    count: 3,
  })
    |> Effect.provideMut(&mut logger)
  if Logger.length(&logger) != usize.ONE {
    return 1
  }
  if Logger.levelAt(&logger, usize.ZERO) != LogLevel.Warning {
    return 2
  }
  return 42
}

effect fn recover(error: LogError) -> i32 {
  return 0
}

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  return run Effect.catchAll(program(), recover)
}
```

## `LogError`

```silk
pub struct LogError
```

A typed failure reported by one [`Logger`](#Logger) provider.

### Details

The numeric code belongs to the provider. Portable code can recover from `LogError` without
assigning one meaning to that code across different providers.

<a id="Logger"></a>

## `Logger`

```silk
pub service Logger
```

A replaceable service that formats and receives one complete semantic log event per call.

### When to use

Use this service when library code must emit events without selecting stdout, memory, or another
destination.

### Details

Each call carries one severity, one static template, and one borrowed argument pack. The service
does not require a newline, timestamp, prefix, allocation, or output destination. The provider
owns those choices and applies the shared `silk.format` contract.

<a id="Logger.log"></a>

### Operation `log`

```silk
effect fn log<Args>(
    level: LogLevel,
    static template: string<'static>,
    args: &Args
  ) -> () ! LogError ? &mut Logger
```

Formats and submits one complete UTF-8 message at one severity to the active provider.

#### Details

Template validation and Display selection match [`Format.format`](./format.md#Format.impl.format). The call does not add a
newline, severity label, timestamp, or provider-independent decoration. A provider failure
produces [`LogError`](#LogError).

```silk

```

Returns the provider-defined failure code for diagnostics.

#### Gotchas

Interpret this code only with knowledge of the selected provider. Different providers can use
the same code for different failures.

<a id="Logger.impl.inMemoryProvider"></a>

### Associated function `inMemoryProvider`

```silk
pub fn inMemoryProvider() -> InMemoryLogger
```

Creates an empty in-memory logger with capacity for eight events and 64 message bytes.

#### Gotchas

A call fails when eight events are already committed. A call also fails when its bytes exceed
the remaining 64-byte total. Neither failure commits the event.

<a id="Logger.impl.inMemoryProviderFailAt"></a>

### Associated function `inMemoryProviderFailAt`

```silk
pub fn inMemoryProviderFailAt(failAt: usize) -> InMemoryLogger
```

Creates an in-memory logger that rejects one zero-based attempted-call ordinal.

#### Details

The configured attempt increases [`attempts`](#Logger.impl.attempts) but does not increase [`length`](#Logger.impl.length) or consume
message capacity. Other attempts retain the eight-event and 64-byte limits of
[`inMemoryProvider`](#Logger.impl.inMemoryProvider).

<a id="Logger.impl.length"></a>

### Method `length`

```silk
pub fn length(self: &InMemoryLogger) -> usize
```

Returns the number of events that the in-memory logger committed.

#### Details

Failed attempts do not increase this count. Use [`attempts`](#Logger.impl.attempts) when rejected calls must also be
observed.

<a id="Logger.impl.levelAt"></a>

### Method `levelAt`

```silk
pub fn levelAt(self: &InMemoryLogger, index: usize) -> LogLevel
```

Returns the severity of one committed event.

#### Gotchas

`index` must be less than [`length`](#Logger.impl.length). An unused index below eight returns the initial Trace
value instead of trapping. An index of eight or more traps.

<a id="Logger.impl.messageLengthAt"></a>

### Method `messageLengthAt`

```silk
pub fn messageLengthAt(self: &InMemoryLogger, index: usize) -> usize
```

Returns the UTF-8 byte length of one committed message.

#### Gotchas

`index` must be less than [`length`](#Logger.impl.length). An unused index below eight returns zero instead of
trapping. An index of eight or more traps.

<a id="Logger.impl.messageByteAt"></a>

### Method `messageByteAt`

```silk
pub fn messageByteAt(
    self: &InMemoryLogger,
    eventIndex: usize,
    byteIndex: usize
  ) -> u8
```

Returns one UTF-8 byte from a committed message.

#### Gotchas

`eventIndex` must be less than [`length`](#Logger.impl.length). `byteIndex` must be less than
[`messageLengthAt`](#Logger.impl.messageLengthAt) for that event. An unused event or invalid byte index traps. An event index
of eight or more also traps.

<a id="InMemoryLogger"></a>

## `InMemoryLogger`

```silk
pub struct InMemoryLogger
```

A deterministic [`Logger`](#Logger) provider that retains up to eight events and 64 total message bytes.

### When to use

Use this provider in tests that must inspect event order, severity, message bytes, or failure
behavior without process output.

### Details

The provider copies each committed message into fixed internal storage. It records attempted
calls separately from committed events. Capacity failure and configured failure do not commit an
event.
